newsitem.title: USA: White House to study Boskin report, other views.
newsitem.headline: White House to study Boskin report, other views.

text.p: A top White House economic adviser said on Wednesday the Clinton administration would study the Boskin committee's report on the consumer price index as well as other views on measuring the cost of living.

"The Clinton administration believes that it is important to have the most accurate measure possible to ensure that Social Security and other benefits are protected from inflation and to adjust tax brackets to keep our tax system fair," Joseph Stiglitz, chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers, said in a statement.
"This measurement must be based on the best scientific and technical judgment that can be broadly agreed to by the nation's top experts at the (Bureau of Labor Statistics) and elsewhere," he added.

"We will carefully review the Boskin report and other evidence regarding the most accurate cost-of-living measure," he said. "The process for improving thsi measure should never be politicized. Our goal should be to reach agreement based on the best scientific and techinal judgment possible."

A congressionally-appointed commission chaired by Michael Boskin, a Stanford University economist, earlier on Wednesday estimated that government statistics overstate inflation by 1.1 percentage points a year, a finding that could have major implications for the federal budget and the whole economy.

The panel recommended a series of actions by the Clinton administration and Congress to fix the problem, including potential legislation to alter the way tax brackets and costly programs like Social Security are adjusted for cost-of-living changes.
